boot_image_write.why: opens a boot partition for writing; the one capability that can leave a locked device unbootable

boot_image_patch.why: builds a modified boot image; the traditional install method this device does not use

boot_image_restore.why: rewrites a boot image from a backup, reachable indirectly from the traditional uninstall path

boot_image_patch_v2.why: second-generation image builder; unnecessary in a late-load-only build

traditional_uninstall.why: the uninstall subcommand reaches image restoration, so it is a boot write path that the operator never asked for by name

ota_slot_control.why: toggles A/B slot state; belongs to OTA install flows, not to loading a module into a running system

root_allowlist_write.why: writes the kernel root allowlist, handing su to a third-party app. This one points the other way from every entry above: it ADDS privilege, and it is at least as consequential as arbitrary_insmod. It is forbidden here before any code for it exists, because the pair this repository ships refuses it anyway - SET_APP_PROFILE is only_manager (dispatch.c:782) and is_manager() is not uid==0 on the shipped .ko - so a candidate that carries it is a candidate whose pair was changed without this gate being revisited. The read-only listing is a separate capability; see PERMITTED.

arbitrary_insmod.why: loads an arbitrary kernel module with kallsyms access; widens kernel modification well past the pinned pair

late_load.why: loads the pinned .ko and runs the late-load stages

kmi_identity.why: selects the embedded module for this kernel; late-load depends on it and it must survive the split from the image-patch code

daemon_install.why: installs the userspace component the late-load stage needs; distinct from the public install subcommand

module_management.why: the module subsystem the CLI administers, which is how this device is managed with no manager installed; evidenced by the install and prune paths, NOT by each individual subcommand

allow_shell.why: lets the shell uid obtain root, which is the only route proven on the device

sepolicy.why: applies the SELinux rules modules and the chain need

metamodule.why: the metamodule and OverlayFS mechanism modules rely on

root_allowlist_read.why: lists the uids the kernel currently allows root (NEW_GET_ALLOW_LIST, UID_GRANTED_ROOT, GET_MANAGER_APPID - all manager_or_root, so root can already do this with no daemon at all). It reads; it cannot grant. On a device managed with no manager installed it is the only way to see a grant left behind by an uninstalled app.

still_owed: a CLI-level refusal test on the candidate: every forbidden subcommand must be unrecognised, which needs a device or emulator
review of the compiled call graph, not only identifier presence
the attestation emitted by the build workflow itself rather than written by hand

rejected_indicators.BLKROSET: a numeric ioctl constant, never a string literal. It is absent from the current shipped daemon, which does contain flash_partition, so treating its absence as evidence would pass the unhardened build.
rejected_indicators.uninstall (bare): matches module uninstall, which is required, as well as the forbidden traditional uninstall. Only the specific help strings distinguish them.
rejected_indicators.slot_suffix: boot-info legitimately reads slot information. Only a write path (post_ota, bootctl) is forbidden.
rejected_indicators.install (bare): matches the required internal daemon installer as well as the public subcommand.
rejected_indicators.manager_appid: already present in the shipped daemon, inside the string ksu_debug_manager_appid, so it cannot witness the grant-listing code either way.
rejected_indicators.allow_su (bindgen field): a field name of struct app_profile. It becomes a string only if something Debug-formats the struct, so its absence would not witness the absence of a write path. Measured zero times in the shipped daemon. The clap-derived allow-su/AllowSu are used instead.

permitted_note: PERMITTED capabilities never change the verdict. They are listed so a passing verdict states which audited capabilities it covers.
doctrine: NO_EVIDENCE is not ABSENT: Rust inlines, and a numeric constant is never a string. Acceptance needs a positive statement from the build, not silence in the binary.
reachability_claim: NOT_ESTABLISHED_BY_THIS_TOOL: an indicator firing proves the code is in the artifact, not that the CLI dispatches to it. A CLI-level refusal test on the candidate is still owed.
